mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.1% indicates an ultra-low interest rate environment that reduces equity discount rates and boosts forward 20-day S&P 500 returns, as observed in historical periods with similar monetary policy settings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in 60% or more of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 1.5% and industrial production (INDPRO) rises above 100, the economy is in a robust expansion phase that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where GDPC1 growth rate > 1.5% and INDPRO > 100 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by housing starts (HOUST) above 900 thousand units and payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 138 million, the S&P 500 typically experiences positive 20-day returns due to sustained consumer spending momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of instances meeting the regime condition over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.5% signals labor market slack that typically precedes monetary policy easing, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where UNRATE > 5.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading exceeding 238.0 indicates accelerating inflation that triggers expectations of monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in 60% or more of instances where CPIAUCSL > 238.0.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is rising above 100 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.1%, the economy is in a low-inflation, high-output phase that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of instances meeting the joint condition over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recovery regime with retail sales (RSAFS) above 425,000 million dollars and industrial production (INDPRO) above 100, the S&P 500 typically generates positive 20-day returns due to strong consumer and business activity.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in 60% or more of instances where RSAFS > 425000 and INDPRO > 100 over a 3-year rolling window.
